# Copilot instructions for OpenNOW

Follow the repository's `AGENTS.md` for architecture, ownership, testing and localization rules.

## Project scope

- The only supported desktop application is `opennow-qt/` (Qt 6, C++20 and QML).
- `native/opennow-core/` owns settings, credentials, GFN orchestration and application services.
- `native/opennow-streamer/` owns the in-process NVST streaming runtime consumed through its C ABI.
- Qt talks to the Rust core through the versioned JSON protocol in `docs/core-protocol.md`.
- The root `package.json` provides optional command aliases and localization tooling. Node is not
  part of the desktop runtime, and there is no Electron application to build or restore.

## Build and checks

Run from the repository root:

```bash
cmake -S opennow-qt -B build/opennow-qt -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build/opennow-qt
ctest --test-dir build/opennow-qt --output-on-failure
cargo test --manifest-path native/opennow-core/Cargo.toml
cargo test --manifest-path native/opennow-streamer/Cargo.toml --workspace
npm run locales:check
```

Run the narrowest affected tests first. For Rust edits, also run the workspace's `cargo fmt`
check and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with `--workspace` for the streamer).
See `opennow-qt/README.md` and `docs/qt-acceptance.md` for smoke and hardware acceptance checks.

## Key conventions

- Keep UI in QML and native integration in narrowly owned C++/Rust types.
- Keep GFN authentication, session refresh and error normalization in the Rust core.
- Update all producers, consumers, fixtures and version checks when changing JSON or C ABI contracts.
- Keep the native video item alive under overlays; handle local shortcuts before gameplay input.
- Preserve legacy data import and stable device IDs when changing persistence.
- Edit only `locales/en.json` for localized copy; other locale files are generated by Crowdin.
